toegepas.voor: Al drie huise in hierdie les
toegepas.na: Al drie die huise in hierdie les
toegepas.rede_vinder: Standard Afrikaans puts the article after 'al' plus a numeral: 'al drie die huise'.
toegepas.fout: 'Al drie huise' leaves out the article that standard Afrikaans uses after 'al' plus a numeral, and reads like a copy of English 'all three houses'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Al drie die huise' is the natural standard form, and the meaning, the quantifier and the protected words are all unchanged.

laat_vaar.blok: Wat 'n huis van gras regop hou
laat_vaar.voor: sit eers 'n raam van stutte op
laat_vaar.na: rig eers 'n raam van stutte op
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Oprig' is the precise verb for erecting a frame; 'opsit' is loose and colloquial.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Sit eers 'n raam van stutte op' is natural, plain Afrikaans and is the finished video's own wording, so swapping it for 'rig op' is a lateral move that would only open a gap between the text and the video.

na_skrywer.voor: 'n Ander naam vir die Zoeloe-grashuis wat "kniel, laat ons bid" beteken.
na_skrywer.na: 'n Ander naam vir die Zoeloe-grashuis. Die naam beteken "kniel, laat ons bid".
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: As written, 'wat' attaches to the nearest noun, so the house rather than the name seems to mean 'kneel, let us pray'.
na_skrywer.fout: In the glossary entry the relative 'wat' comes straight after 'Zoeloe-grashuis', so on a first reading it can seem to be the house, not the name, that means 'kniel, laat ons bid'; and a glossary entry is read on its own.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The ambiguity is real, but the proposal rewrites a [begrip] definition into two sentences, which goes beyond a spelling or grammar fix, so the writer should resolve it and keep the study text and the entry in line.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Ouers wys dit vir hulle kinders
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Ouers wys dit aan hulle kinders
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Standard written Afrikaans shows something 'aan' someone; 'wys vir' is colloquial.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Iets vir iemand wys' is natural, accepted Afrikaans with the same meaning, so the swap is lateral.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: stut die dak van onder af.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The idiomatic form is 'van onder af'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'stut die dak van onder' is already natural and clear, so adding 'af' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: wat tot op die grond kom
laat_vaar_vorige.na: wat tot op die grond strek
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Strek' is the natural verb for a shape that reaches down to the ground.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'tot op die grond kom' is natural Afrikaans and plainer for a Grade 4 reader than 'strek'.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Avoids repeating 'hulle eie' twice in one sentence; the first 'eie naam' carries the point.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'hulle eie taal' is a fixed expression that stresses the contrast with the Afrikaans name and matches the glossary entry, so dropping 'eie' loses emphasis for little gain.
